analysis.title: CIO View: Listed real estate
key_insights: UBS CIO favors listed real estate companies that pursue growth, make acquisitions through accretive issuance, and show strong pricing power, profitable pipelines, attractive yield gaps and robust cash flows.
UBS stays selective on companies trading at a discount to net asset value (NAV), which may be value traps unless they grow their businesses.

UBS expects overall real estate values to keep appreciating over the medium term with further rental growth. Higher interest and opportunity costs may weigh on valuations of non-core properties in the short term.
Global direct real estate transaction volumes rose about 15% y/y last year, and UBS expects similar growth in 2026. Third-quarter quarterly volumes were the highest since 2021.

Listed real estate outperformed equities early in 2026 on defensive characteristics and rate-cut expectations. Volatility returned as long-term US bond markets sold off. The year is repeating 2025, with the sector underperforming while tech and AI firms attract capital.

Tariffs are no longer a significant headwind for industrial real estate, particularly given the data center boom. Real estate stocks should stay volatile, with potential to rebound once inflation is perceived to have peaked.

A steeper US yield curve is not necessarily negative, since the implication depends on whether it reflects a stronger economy or tighter liquidity. The earlier curve inversion was a key factor in the sector's underperformance versus global equities.

UBS thinks investors may be underestimating supply constraints across real estate markets. Exceptions are US Sun Belt residential, US West Coast office and Hong Kong office, where conditions are improving.
Global listed real estate trades at an estimated discount to NAV of about 6% as of 16 November 2026. REITs trade at a 2% premium to NAV on UBS estimates.
Senior housing, lodging, retail and self-storage are outperforming. Residential, office and industrial are lagging.
UBS expects listed real estate EPS growth of 11% in 2026 and 7.4% in 2027, excluding emerging markets, driven by rental indexation, reversion and selective transactions and acquisitions.
The global average dividend yield is 3.4%, below the seven-year average of 3.6%. The 12-month forward P/E is in line with the long-term average of 14-15x.

Regional preferences: US attractive on robust fundamentals after rates already rose significantly. Continental Europe looks cheap. Asia has a mixed preference for developers and REITs. Australia's outlook for 2027 improved on a peak in rates and lower financing cost pressure.
Index targets: FTSE EPRA/Nareit Developed at 7,028 on 17 Nov 26, forecast 8,000 Mar 27, 8,400 Jun 27, 8,600 Sep 27, 8,800 Dec 27. Upside scenario Dec 27 target 9,100, downside 8,500.

sector_views.rationale: Robust fundamentals, rental growth and resilient transaction volumes, though rate volatility and deep-discount valuations warrant selectivity.
These subsectors are lagging. Residential and office also face supply and demand issues in specific regions.

earnings_insights: UBS expects listed real estate EPS growth of 11% in 2026 and 7.4% in 2027, excluding emerging markets (forecast).
UBS expects no further improvement in earnings growth ahead but sees attractive growth continuing. Earnings growth has been robust in 2026 despite higher financing costs.

risk_factors: Higher government bond yields and volatile bond markets raise opportunity costs and risk premiums.
Capitalization rates stay high amid elevated risk premiums and slowing rental growth, preventing property values from rising.
Weak rental reversions, tenant renewal incentives and stagnating occupancy dampen income growth.
Discounted companies may be value traps if they cannot grow.
Open-ended funds facing redemptions are likely to sell properties.
The 2020 submarket dislocation fails to revert, particularly for secondary offices.
vol_and_positioning: Real estate stocks are expected to remain volatile, with potential to rebound once inflation is perceived to have peaked.
UBS stays cautious on deep discount valuations in some names due to volatile bond market conditions.
geopolitical: The report cites ongoing geopolitical tensions as a factor in higher risk premiums in listed real estate.
Trade uncertainty has receded and tariffs are no longer a significant headwind for industrial real estate.

tension_points.bull_case: Rental growth, resilient transaction volumes, 11% EPS growth in 2026 and a 6% NAV discount support a rebound toward the 9,100 upside target.
tension_points.bear_case: High bond yields and risk premiums keep cap rates elevated and rental growth slows, leaving the index near the 8,500 downside target.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cap rates stay high amid elevated risk premiums, with weak rental reversions and stagnating occupancy preventing property value gains.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rental growth, resilient transaction volumes and mildly attractive earnings yields support the sector despite bond yield volatility.
theme_stances.evidence: Earnings yields from listed companies relative to equities are mildly attractive
